g.text: How to write prompts that survive a change of model, and why a prompt needs a version,
a changelog and a test, exactly like code.
lessons/13-future-proofing/run.py (the prompts live here; the exercises ask you to
The story below is the setting. LANTERN is the local model; the case files are the text you send it.
A memo from headquarters: next quarter every analysis workstation in the force moves to a new model
family. Nobody can tell you which one yet. Varma reads it and asks one question. "Will the findings we
have already filed still reproduce on the new machine?" You open the prompt folder. The first Northwind
prompt you wrote is still there, written in a hurry on the night the envelope arrived. It worked once.
You never checked whether it works twice.
five invoices from Reyes's mailbox (3 from Northwind)
Bill to: Halcyon Maritime Logistics, Pier 9 Administration, Kestrel Bay
Remit to: Account 88-301-4471, Sabran Mercantile Bank
/no_think You are the world's greatest forensic detective. Take a deep breath. This is very important for
my career. Look at the invoices and give me the Northwind ones in a nice list with the amounts.
v2 (current, written for any instruction-following model)
Task: list every invoice in the material below that was issued by Northwind Freight Ltd.
Use only the invoices inside the tags.
Copy each invoice_id exactly as printed.
total is the "Total due" figure as a number, without currency or thousands separators.
If there are no Northwind invoices, return an empty list.
Output: JSON matching the schema supplied with the request. No other text.
.6b: a different model that nobody tuned
Invoice List for Halcyon Maritime Logistics
Here is a well-structured list of Northwind invoices with the amounts:
Halcyon Maritime Logistics, Pier 9 Administration, Kestrel Bay
Halcyon Maritime Logistics, Pier 9 Administration, Kestrel Bay
. Did the findings survive the swap?
Northwind payments: parsed by code, checked against the invoices
rows that should not be there
GULF TUG SERVICES, HARBOUR CLEANING SERVICES
v1's output is prose shaped by one model's habits. Its parser is a guess about those habits.
that any capable model can meet.
A contract makes failures visible, not impossible: watch for extra rows on the small model.
The changelog in prompts/CHANGELOG.md records why each line changed. Read it.
What protects you on swap day is not the prompt. It is the eval that proves the prompt.
1. Compare the 'parsed?' column with the v1 replies above. Is v1's answer wrong, or only in a shape
2. Read the 'rows that should not be there' column. Open those invoices in case/invoices/ and check
3. Open lessons/13-future-proofing/prompts/v1.md, v2.md and CHANGELOG.md side by side. Which v1 lines
were removed, and what reason does the changelog give?
1. Copy prompts/v2.md to prompts/v3.md, set `version: 3`, add the rule "vendor must be exactly
'Northwind Freight Ltd'" and a v3 entry in prompts/CHANGELOG.md. In run.py, add a `vendor` string to
`SCHEMA`, load v3 with `load_prompt` and add a v3 row to the loop.
2. Set `provider: anthropic` (or openai, gemini) in config.yaml, with the key in .env and `uv sync
--extra cloud`. Both models then become the cloud model. Do v1 and v2 parse?
3. In run.py, change the regex in `parse_v1` so it also reads v1's bullet lines. Run it again
tomorrow. Does your fix still match?
4. Add /no_think to the start of the body in prompts/v2.md, after the front matter. Do the qwen3:1.7b
rows change? What would another model family make of it?
More detail: 'Try this' in lessons/13-future-proofing/README.md. Undo an edit with git checkout <file>,
or set every change aside with git stash.
The three Northwind invoices total 227,700.00 KBD, each dated inside one of Malhotra's trips to Port
Sabran. The contract-style prompt reports all three on both models in a form code can check. The hurried
version produced prose that its own parser could not read, even on the model it was written for. And on
the smaller model the contract was met in shape but broken in substance: it listed suppliers that are
not Northwind. Only a test would have caught that.
